questions.q: What problem does a remote backend solve that local state can't?
options: It automatically writes your resource blocks for you
It eliminates the need for a provider block
It makes terraform apply run faster
It gives the whole team one shared, durable copy of state instead of a file on one person's disk
questions.explain: Every teammate who runs terraform init against the same backend connects to the exact same state — there's no file to pass around.

questions.q: In a backend "azurerm" block, what does the container_name argument identify?
options: The name of the Azure subscription
The Docker container running Terraform
The blob container inside the Storage Account where state files are stored
The resource group that holds the virtual network
questions.explain: container_name is the blob container; key is the specific state blob inside it for this project.

questions.q: In a backend "s3" block with bucket, key, and region set, what does key represent?
options: The object path within the bucket for this specific project's state file
The DynamoDB table name used for locking
An AWS access key used to authenticate
The encryption key used to encrypt the bucket
questions.explain: key is the object path, like app-prod/terraform.tfstate, letting one bucket hold many projects' state side by side.

questions.q: What happens when you run terraform init after adding a backend block to a project that already has local state?
options: Terraform deletes the local state file automatically with no prompt
Terraform prompts you to copy the existing local state up to the newly configured backend
Terraform ignores the new backend block until the next major version
Terraform recreates all resources from scratch
questions.explain: Answering yes to that prompt migrates your existing state to the remote backend without touching real infrastructure.

questions.q: After state has been migrated to a remote backend, is it still necessary to commit terraform.tfstate to git?
options: It becomes required once a remote backend is configured
Yes — it must now be committed so teammates can see the migration happened
No — the local file is no longer the source of truth and should still be excluded from git
Yes, but only on the main branch
questions.explain: The remote backend is now the source of truth; the local file remains unnecessary and unsafe to commit, same as before.
